All right, the latest tool run just confirmed that the memory subsystem is persisting data correctly. The `~/.glint/memory.md` file now contains the line:

- The user's favorite color is orange. _(2026-06-12)_

That matches exactly what I instructed the TUI to remember with the `/remember` command earlier. The TUI also echoed back “Your favorite color has been recorded as orange.” and then “Your favorite color is orange.” confirming the round‑trip from user input to memory write and back to retrieval. So the end‑to‑end flow—input → memory write → memory read → display—is functioning as intended.

While reviewing the TUI output, I noticed the phrase “has been recorded” appearing in the response. My existing premature‑claim regex was designed to catch statements where the agent claims to have performed an action before actually doing it (e.g., “I have already searched the web”). However, the pattern didn’t catch this phrasing because it was looking for “recorded” only in certain contexts. This slipped through the earlier test suite, so I should extend the regex to also flag “has been recorded” or similar constructions that could mislead the user into thinking something is done when it’s not.

Now that memory is verified and the regex tweak is identified, the next logical steps are to test the other major capabilities: web search and sub‑agent orchestration. I’ll need to run a web search command, verify that the results are captured correctly, and then spin up a sub‑agent (e.g., a browser or calculator) to ensure that inter‑agent communication works. Those tests will round out the validation of the full feature set.

Given all that, I should report back to the user that memory works, note the regex improvement, and state the plan to move on to web search and sub‑agent tests. That concise status update will keep the user informed and set expectations for the next actions.

Thus, the appropriate next message is:
“Memory works end-to-end. Extending the premature-claim regex (caught "has been recorded" slipping through), then web search + subagent tests.”
